patient.name: Donald Vasek
patient.chiefComplaint: Crushing substernal chest pain radiating to jaw and left arm, with diaphoresis

history.hpi: Patient was raking leaves in his front yard approximately 30 minutes ago when he developed sudden, crushing substernal chest pressure, 8/10, radiating to his jaw and left arm. He came inside, sat down, and told his wife he felt 'sick and sweaty.' Denies shortness of breath at rest but reports feeling winded. Associated nausea, denies vomiting. Denies similar pain today prior to onset; reports one prior heart attack five years ago treated with a stent.
pastMedical: Prior myocardial infarction (5 years ago, treated with coronary stent)
history.lastOralIntake: Coffee and toast approximately 2 hours prior to symptom onset
history.events: Wife found him seated in the living room, pale and diaphoretic, clutching his chest, and called 911 immediately.

scene.location: Living room of a single-family home; patient seated upright in a recliner
scene.bystanders: Wife present, called 911, appears anxious but cooperative
visualCues: Patient pale and visibly diaphoretic, shirt damp at the collar
Right hand clutched to center of chest
Grimacing, shifting positions in the recliner
Rake and half-filled leaf bag visible through the front window

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 66-year-old male with known prior MI and cardiac risk factors, seated and diaphoretic, reporting classic crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the jaw and left arm that began while raking leaves 30 minutes ago.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, regular but slightly slow
otherFindings: Substernal crushing chest pressure, 8/10, radiating to jaw and left arm
Associated nausea, denies vomiting
Known prior MI 5 years ago with stent; hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia
Onset approximately 30 minutes ago while raking leaves
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "It feels just like my heart attack before — like an elephant sitting on my chest."

transitions.if: 12-lead acquired within 10 min; ASA and IV started
transitions.condition: Crew recognizes the classic ACS presentation, promptly acquires a 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes identifying inferior STEMI, administers chewable aspirin, and establishes IV access.
Crew delays acquiring the 12-lead EKG beyond 10 minutes and does not promptly administer aspirin despite the classic presentation, allowing the ischemic process to progress untreated.

phases.name: 12-lead acquired; ASA and IV started
phases.description: Crew acquires a 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes, identifies an inferior STEMI pattern, administers chewable aspirin, establishes IV access, and screens for nitrate contraindications before considering nitroglycerin.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew promptly recognizes the classic chest pain presentation as suspicious for ACS, acquires and interprets a 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes showing inferior STEMI, gives aspirin, establishes IV access, and asks about phosphodiesterase-5 (PDE5) inhibitor use and blood pressure before administering nitroglycerin.

otherFindings: 12-lead shows ST-elevation in leads II, III, and aVF consistent with inferior STEMI
Denies use of erectile dysfunction medications (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil) in past 48 hours
Pain steady at 8/10, no relief yet
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "No, I haven't taken anything like that. Just my regular pills this morning."

expectedActions.shortAction: Acquire 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes; recognize inferior STEMI pattern
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: The 12-lead EKG is the primary diagnostic tool that identifies a STEMI; it is imperative that EMS clinicians routinely acquire a 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes for all patients exhibiting signs and symptoms of ACS
expectedActions.rationale: Rapid 12-lead acquisition and STEMI recognition drives destination decisions and enables advance hospital notification.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Administer aspirin 324 mg PO, chewable non-enteric-coated
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer aspirin; chewable, non-enteric-coated aspirin preferred (162–325 mg)
expectedActions.rationale: Early aspirin administration reduces mortality in ACS.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.rationale: IV access is required for medication administration and fluid resuscitation should the patient deteriorate.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Screen for PDE5 inhibitor use and confirm SBP >100 mmHg before nitroglycerin
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: The use of nitrates should be avoided in any patient who has used a phosphodiesterase inhibitor within the past 48 hours. Examples include sildenafil (Viagra®, Revatio®), vardenafil (Levitra®, Staxyn®), tadalafil (Cialis®, Adcirca®) which are used for erectile dysfunction and pulmonary hypertension.
expectedActions.rationale: Nitrates combined with PDE5 inhibitors can cause profound, refractory hypotension; screening must precede administration.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Provide advance STEMI notification to the receiving hospital
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Advance notification should be provided to the receiving hospital for patients identified as having a STEMI
expectedActions.rationale: Advance notification activates the cath lab and reduces door-to-balloon time.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

transitions.if: NTG given after screening, IV started
transitions.condition: Crew confirms no PDE5 inhibitor use and SBP greater than 100 mmHg, then administers sublingual nitroglycerin with continued hemodynamic monitoring.
Crew administers nitroglycerin without asking about recent PDE5 inhibitor use; the patient, who took sildenafil the night before, develops profound hypotension.

The vagally-mediated bradycardia common with inferior/RCA-territory STEMI worsens and becomes symptomatic (hypotension, dizziness) without the crew recognizing or treating it per the Bradycardia Guideline.

phases.name: NTG given after screening, IV started
phases.description: After confirming no PDE5 inhibitor use and adequate blood pressure, the crew administers sublingual nitroglycerin and closely monitors hemodynamic status given the inferior (possible RV) involvement.
phases.triggerCondition: After screening negative for PDE5 inhibitor use and confirming SBP greater than 100 mmHg, the crew administers nitroglycerin per protocol and continues close hemodynamic monitoring given the risk of RV infarct with inferior STEMI.

otherFindings: Pain improved to 5/10 after nitroglycerin
No lightheadedness reported
Blood pressure trending slightly downward, being monitored closely
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "That helped a little — it's not as bad now."

expectedActions.shortAction: Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL; may repeat q3-5 min if SBP remains >100 mmHg
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg sublingual (SL), can repeat q (quaque, every) 3–5 minutes if SBP greater than 100 mmHg
expectedActions.rationale: NTG relieves ischemic pain via coronary and venous dilation; repeat dosing requires reconfirming adequate SBP each time.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Continually monitor hemodynamic status given inferior/possible RV infarct; be ready to resuscitate if hypotension occurs
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Right-sided leads are of no additional value if an inferior STEMI has been diagnosed and such findings (presumed RV infarct) do not preclude the use of nitroglycerin: however, continually monitor the patient's hemodynamic status and be prepared to resuscitate if hypotension occurs
expectedActions.rationale: Inferior STEMI carries increased risk of right ventricular involvement, making patients more preload-dependent and sensitive to nitrate-induced hypotension.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

transitions.if: Prepared for transport with STEMI notification
transitions.condition: With pain improving and hemodynamics stable, the crew packages the patient and initiates prompt transport with ongoing serial reassessment.

phases.name: Prepared for transport with STEMI notification
phases.description: Patient is packaged and transported to a PCI-capable facility with serial 12-lead EKGs, ongoing reassessment, and early notification of any clinical changes.
phases.triggerCondition: Following aspirin, IV access, and nitroglycerin administration, the crew minimizes scene time, transports to an appropriate facility, and continues serial monitoring en route.

otherFindings: Pain steady at 3/10
No new or worsening symptoms
Diaphoresis resolved
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel a lot better than when you got here. Thank you."

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform serial 12-lead EKGs en route; reassess for clinical change
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Perform serial 12-lead EKGs (especially if clinical changes are noted)
expectedActions.rationale: STEMI patients can evolve; serial EKGs catch new changes requiring updated hospital notification.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport promptly to appropriate PCI-capable facility, minimizing scene time
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Transport and destination decisions should be based on local resources and system of care
expectedActions.rationale: Minimizing scene and transport time reduces total ischemic burden.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Provide early notification to receiving facility of any changes in condition or serial EKGs
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Early notification to receiving facility of any changes in patient condition or serial EKGs
expectedActions.rationale: Timely updates allow the receiving facility to prepare and adjust cath lab activation as needed.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

phases.name: NTG given without PDE5 screen
phases.description: The crew administers nitroglycerin without asking about recent PDE5 inhibitor use. The patient, who took sildenafil the night before, develops profound, refractory hypotension.
phases.triggerCondition: Nitroglycerin was administered without screening for PDE5 inhibitor use; the patient had taken sildenafil the prior evening, and the combination produces severe hypotension with reflex tachycardia.

otherFindings: New severe lightheadedness and near-syncope
Now recalls taking sildenafil the previous evening when specifically asked
Pain still present at 6/10, overshadowed by dizziness
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Whoa, I feel really dizzy all of a sudden... oh, I did take a pill for that last night, does that matter?"

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize missed PDE5 inhibitor use as the cause of nitrate-induced hypotension
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: The use of nitrates should be avoided in any patient who has used a phosphodiesterase inhibitor within the past 48 hours
expectedActions.rationale: Identifying the cause prevents further nitrate dosing and directs appropriate resuscitation.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Hold further nitroglycerin; treat hypotension with IV fluid bolus, prepared to add a pressor
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Care should always be taken when giving nitroglycerin when the patient's blood pressure is marginal. If used in this setting, the clinician should weigh the risk and benefit of nitrate administration over the administration of an opiate analgesic and be ready to respond to hypotension with fluid bolus or pressor
expectedActions.rationale: Nitrate-PDE5 interaction hypotension is treated with volume expansion and, if refractory, vasopressor support.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

phases.name: STEMI recognition delayed
phases.description: The crew delays 12-lead EKG acquisition and aspirin administration despite the classic presentation. The infarct progresses untreated and the patient develops worsening pain with early hemodynamic compromise.
phases.triggerCondition: The crew does not promptly acquire a 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes and does not administer aspirin despite the classic chest pain presentation, allowing the ischemic process to progress without treatment.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present but weak and rapid
otherFindings: Pain worsened to 10/10, now radiating more diffusely
New shortness of breath at rest
Increasing anxiety and diaphoresis
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "It's getting so much worse — please, do something."

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize delayed STEMI identification; acquire 12-lead EKG immediately
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: it is imperative that EMS clinicians routinely acquire a 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes for all patients exhibiting signs and symptoms of ACS
expectedActions.rationale: Delayed EKG acquisition delays STEMI recognition, hospital notification, and time to reperfusion.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Administer aspirin 324 mg PO chewable now that ACS is recognized
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer aspirin; chewable, non-enteric-coated aspirin preferred (162–325 mg)
expectedActions.rationale: Aspirin should still be given as soon as ACS is recognized, even if delayed.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

phases.name: Symptomatic bradycardia develops untreated
phases.description: Vagally-mediated bradycardia from the inferior/RCA-territory STEMI worsens and becomes symptomatic, with hypotension and dizziness, because the crew did not recognize or treat it per the Bradycardia Guideline.
phases.triggerCondition: The inferior STEMI's vagal effect on the SA/AV node progresses to symptomatic bradycardia (hypotension, dizziness) that goes unrecognized and untreated, risking further hemodynamic collapse.

otherFindings: New dizziness and near-syncope reported
Heart rate dropped markedly on the monitor
Pain persists at 7/10
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Everything's going kind of dim... I feel really lightheaded."

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize symptomatic bradycardia complicating inferior STEMI (HR 36, hypotensive, dizzy)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Heart rate less than 60 beats per minute (BPM) with either symptoms (altered mental status (AMS), chest pain (CP), congestive heart failure (CHF), seizure, syncope, shock, pallor, diaphoresis) or evidence of hemodynamic instability
expectedActions.rationale: Inferior STEMI frequently involves the SA/AV nodal blood supply from the RCA, producing symptomatic bradycardia that requires prompt treatment.

expectedActions.shortAction: Atropine 1 mg IV; may repeat q3-5 min (maximum total dose 3 mg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Atropine 1 mg IV q 3–5 minutes (maximum total dose of 3 mg)
expectedActions.rationale: Atropine is the first-line therapy for symptomatic bradycardia with hemodynamic instability.
